text.p: Italian bonds and futures, which ended the week with net gains, flattened out recent progress for a bout of consolidation to end a few ticks down on the day.

Dealers had plenty to chew on with Germany's plan to revalue its gold reserves in a bid to meet criteria for joining a single European currency, nervousness over U.S. interest rates and with upcoming Italian inflation data due next week.

June Btp futures on LIFFE exercised strength up to 130.74 earlier before U.S. data and weaker Bunds combined to undermine progress, dealers said. On the cash market the February 2007 Btp ended four basis points down at 97.41.
The June future was six basis points in the red at the finish at 130.18. "As long as we close above the 130 level then the positive trend is still valid," a broker in London said.

A rate cut in Spain helped feed hopes that Italy might see its way to following suit towards the end of the month. Next Tuesday and Wednesday brings preliminary inflation data from 11 sample cities, with analysts forecasting a year on year rate of 1.5 percent after April's 1.7 percent.
The government's three-year economic plan (Dpef) is also due next week and could help prompt the Bank of Italy into easing. In any case, hope of a cut continue to buoy the market.

Germany's plan to revalue gold reserves found mixed views. On one hand dealers said Bonn seemed determined not to let momentum for EMU flag. On the other it moved the goal posts in terms of EMU criteria, potentially softening the requirements and so EMU. "Generally it may not be such a good thing for Europe," a broker said but added it kept up EMU momentum.

"Market opinion on EMU and Italy changes often," another said, but added at the moment Italy's chances of joining with the first wave looked a bit better. Accordingly, the Btp-Bund spread narrowed to 146 basis points for the first time using the February 2007 Btp and the July 2004 Bund.--Milan +392 66129507
